cloud.title: Danfoss Ally Cloud — account
cloud.description: Sign in with your Danfoss Ally app account — the same email and password you use in the app. No developer account, API key or traffic capture is required.

data_description.username: The email address of your Danfoss Ally / Smart Life app account.
data_description.country_code: The country of your app account. The datacenter is derived from it automatically.
data_description.region: Leave on "Automatic": the datacenter is derived from your country. Only change it if your account lives in a different Tuya datacenter.
data_description.manual_secrets: Leave unticked: the integration derives the signing material itself. Tick only if sign-in is refused although your email and password are correct (e.g. after a new app version) and you have captured sign_key, deviceId and chKey from the app.

cloud_secrets.title: Danfoss Ally Cloud — installation secrets
cloud_secrets.description: Advanced fallback. Normally the integration derives these values itself; enter them only if the automatic sign-in was refused. They are captured from the app's network traffic (see the documentation), stored with the entry and never shown again or logged.

data_description.sign_key: The sign_key captured from the app (starts with "com.danfoss.ally_").
data_description.device_id: The deviceId captured from the app.
data_description.ch_key: The chKey captured from the app.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in again to Danfoss Ally (Cloud)
reauth_confirm.description: The Danfoss Ally account refused the sign-in (password changed, or installation secrets no longer valid). Enter the password of the same account. Fill in the sign key, device id or channel key only if they changed: left empty, the current value is kept.

data.sign_key: Sign key (sign_key) — only if it changed
data.device_id: Device id (deviceId) — only if it changed
data.ch_key: Channel key (chKey) — only if it changed

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Danfoss Ally (Cloud)
reconfigure.description: Update the country, datacenter, password or installation secrets. Leave any secret field empty to keep the current value.

data.sign_key: Sign key (sign_key) — only if it changed
data.device_id: Device id (deviceId) — only if it changed
data.ch_key: Channel key (chKey) — only if it changed

data_description.region: Leave on "Automatic" to derive the datacenter from the country.

companion.title: Danfoss Ally Companion (MQTT)
companion.description: Connect to one or more Zigbee2MQTT-compatible bridges on Home Assistant's Mosquitto broker (e.g. zigbee2mqtt, danfoss2mqtt). No cloud credentials required.

error.empty_prefixes: Specify at least one MQTT prefix (e.g. zigbee2mqtt)
error.invalid_auth: Sign-in refused: check the email, password and country (or the manually entered installation secrets)

abort.wrong_account: This is not the account of this entry: sign in with the same account, or add the other account as a new entry

data.distinct_device_id: Use a dedicated device id (coexist with the Danfoss app / MCP connector without logging each other out)
data.enable_local: Enable the local Zigbee tunnel (gateways) for writes the cloud misses
data.local_supervised_settings: Supervised trial — head settings written through the LOCAL TUNNEL, NOT yet validated on real hardware, opened for a first write done in person on a test head (see docs/first-write-procedure.md). Needs the local tunnel. Leave empty otherwise
data.local_supervised_head: Supervised trial — the ONE test head the local-tunnel settings ticked above open on. Every other head gets no write entity. Leave on — when no trial is running: nothing is then open
data.post_command_refresh: Refresh just-commanded heads via the per-device route (R-3: the bulk poll lags for minutes after a change). Off by default — turn on for a real-hardware validation session
data.enable_vacation_write: Enable vacation writes (holiday set/cancel). Off by default — turn on only for a supervised real-hardware validation
data.enable_head_unbind: Enable device unbind (disconnect a head, sensor or relay from the network). Destructive — off by default; turn on only for a supervised real-hardware validation
data.enable_cloud_mqtt: Enable the Tuya cloud MQTT channel (experimental, unofficial): writes the settings of a head that is in no room. Off by default — keeps a connection open to the Tuya broker on your account
data.cloud_mqtt_supervised_dps: Supervised trial — settings NOT yet validated on the Tuya cloud MQTT channel, opened for a first write done in person on a test head (see docs/first-write-procedure.md). Leave empty otherwise
data.cloud_mqtt_supervised_head: Supervised trial — the ONE test head the settings ticked above open on (an isolated head). Every other head keeps its normal routing. Leave on — when no trial is running: nothing is then open
data.cloud_mqtt_probe: Measure what the Tuya cloud MQTT broker pushes (listen-only, nothing is sent to the heads; aggregates in the diagnostics). Off by default — opens a broker connection on your account, closes itself after 48 h
data.mqtt_mode: MQTT publishing: off, discovery (auto HA entities), zigbee2mqtt (z2m-compatible topics)
data.mqtt_source: Source of published values: cloud or local

companion.title: Companion options
companion.description: Periodic writes from the Companion to the Zigbee2MQTT heads of a virtual room. Each one stays closed unless ticked. Closing one sends nothing: the heads keep the last value they received (a head drops a room-sensor value by itself after 35 minutes or 3 hours).

data.companion_feed_external_sensor: Feed each virtual room's sensor temperature to its heads (external_measured_room_sensor): on a change of 0.2 °C or every 20 minutes, at most once every 5 minutes per head
data.companion_feed_load_mean: Write the room's mean load to its heads (load_room_mean) — NOT validated on real hardware. Only for rooms of two heads or more where every head reports load_balancing_enable on

error.empty_prefixes: Specify at least one MQTT prefix (e.g. zigbee2mqtt)

duplicate_cloud_provider.title: Danfoss Ally: duplicate provider active
duplicate_cloud_provider.description: The Danfoss Ally **Companion** (zigbee2mqtt / danfoss2mqtt) is running, but another Danfoss Ally **direct-cloud** entry is also active. Both provide the same heads, so every head gets duplicate entities (the `_2` / `_3` entity-id suffixes). Make the Companion the sole provider: disable or remove the old direct-cloud entry, and stop any MQTT-discovery bridge still publishing the same heads. Step-by-step guide: `docs/v2-cutover.md`. This warning clears automatically once the old entry is gone.
